title: What Is an API?

tldr.In one line: An API is a contract that lets one program ask another to do something without knowing how it works inside — so both sides can change independently.
tldr.In plain English: Think of a wall socket: you plug in a lamp without knowing anything about the power station. The shape of the socket is the promise. A web API is the same kind of promise between two programs, sent over the internet using HTTP.
tldr.You'll be able to: Explain what an API is (and isn't) in one sentence · Spot the client, the contract and the server in any app you use · Read a basic HTTP request and its JSON response

svgs.alt: Diagram: a client app talks to the server only through the API contract, like a diner using a menu and a waiter

takeaways: An API is a defined contract that lets one system ask another to do something without knowing its internals.
This handbook focuses on **web APIs**: HTTP-based client/server request/response systems.
The value of an API is decoupling — the caller and the provider can change independently as long as the contract holds.
LLM APIs, RAG APIs, and agent/MCP systems are still APIs in exactly this sense — they just happen to have a language model as the "kitchen."
